feedback: Written before this candidate has raced; no outcome is claimed for it. Your hold of the iteration-10 geometry is supported by the evidence. Span (40 to 60 mm), forward position (0.04 to 0.075 m), footprint (12 and 16 mm), track width (0.10 and 0.12 m) and mass (0.5 and 0.6 kg) were each tried around this layout. Iteration 5 (60 mm span) and iteration 6 (16 mm footprint) both cost oval finishes, and iteration 7 (0.10 m track) also lost them. Iteration 8 showed mass 0.5 kg kept the oval finishes (16 of 20), and iteration 10 (546.4) showed the controller was the lever that moved the bends. The s-bend line loss fell from 2.3 (iteration 9) to 1.5 (iteration 10), so the controller, not geometry, is still the lever. Because this is the final iteration, no later race can use a geometry change. Record these as the last observations: if the unseen-track score is well below the development results, check whether the s-bend loss on the held-back track is at 2.0 or more, which would point to wheel_track 0.14 m as the untested geometry direction.
requested_changes: Hold the iteration-10 geometry (x = plus or minus 0.025 m, y = 0.075 m, 12 mm footprint, wheel_track 0.12 m, mass 0.5 kg) as proposed; no further change is possible after this iteration.

If future work resumes from this geometry, test wheel_track 0.14 m only if s-bend line_loss_events stays at 2.0 or more, since the 0.10 m track (iteration 7) was the only narrower track tried and lost the oval finishes.
Keep the 50 mm span and 12 mm footprint, because widening the span to 60 mm and enlarging the footprint to 16 mm each cost oval finishes (iterations 5 and 6).
